title: Default OpenXR Action Map causes errors when enabling eye tracking
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in Godot 4.5.1.stable

### System information

Windows 10 - Godot v4.5.1.stable - Vulkan (Mobile)

### Issue description

When I enable eye tracking for a project with the default Action Map and on a machine with the `XR_EXT_eye_gaze_interaction` extension installed, OpenXR rapidly emits `XR_ERROR_HANDLE_INVALID` errors at runtime.

~~I have isolated the problem to an inappropriate entry in the default "HTC Vive tracker" profile.~~

~~The fix should be as simple as removing `"/user/eyes_ext"` from the [default "HTC Vive tracker" profile entry](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/modules/openxr/action_map/openxr_action_map.cpp#L234), as there is no way (that I am aware of, at least) for an HTC Vive tracker to provide eye tracking data.~~

Note that this problem only effects the default, pre-written `openxr_action_map`, ~~as generating a new "HTC Vive tracker" profile [does not feature this erroneous entry](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/modules/openxr/extensions/openxr_htc_vive_tracker_extension.cpp#L116).~~

~~You can verify the change is isolated to that single removal by running:~~  
~~`git diff --word-diff=plain --no-index ./openxr_action_map.tres ./openxr_action_map_fix.tres`~~

~~If this seems acceptable to seasoned eyes, I would be very excited to contribute my first PR to Godot with this fix :)~~

### Steps to reproduce

Based on the source of the issue, I assume it is caused by any runtime with the `XR_EXT_eye_gaze_interaction` extension installed, but the below instructions will be a way to reproduce it with OpenXR API Layers provided by Vive Console for SteamVR.

> [!WARNING]
> **If you do not already use Vive Console, I do not recommend installing it on your primary development machine for this test.  It risks making persistent changes to the Windows registry that are very frustrating to remove after uninstallation - so testing on a temporary install of Windows is highly recommended!**
>
> If you want to proceed on your primary machine anyway, then I recommend after uninstallation searching the registery for keys containing the word "VIVE", and deleting them.

## Required setup
- Windows (10) running SteamVR as the OpenXR runtime
- A SteamVR-compatible headset (with or without eye-tracking) *(example: Valve Index)*

## Reproduction steps
- Verify in SteamVR settings > OpenXR that no OpenXR API Layers are installed (or, disable them if they are)
- Install [Vive Console for SteamVR](https://store.steampowered.com/app/1635730/VIVE_Console_for_SteamVR/) *(I use the beta branch)*
- Run the installed software at least once
- Verify in SteamVR settings > OpenXR that there are now 3 OpenXR API Layers installed:
  - ViveVR OpenXR Hand Tracking
  - ViveVR OpenXR SRWorks
  - Vive OpenXR Facial Tracking
- Disable the other OpenXR API Layers so that only "Vive OpenXR Facial Tracking" is active
- Launch the bare-minimum godot project below
- Observe the firehose of OpenXR errors (`XR_ERROR_HANDLE_INVALID`)

~~## Solution~~
- ~~Change Project Settings > XR > OpenXR > Default Action Map to `res://openxr_action_map_fix.tres`~~
- ~~Run the project~~
- ~~Note the lack of errors~~

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[eye-tracking-mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24016631/eye-tracking-mrp.zip)
